Create a dense central Paris district under quiet overcast light, with roughly twenty tightly packed perimeter blocks following narrow angled streets and wider avenues. Use irregular polygonal footprints, wedge corners, and enclosed courtyards, some with unfinished blank off-white walls. Make buildings predominantly six to seven stories, with pale weathered stone, tall windows, iron balconies, mansard roofs, dormers, and chimneys. Add asphalt roads, broad stone sidewalks, crossings, lane markings, and traffic islands. Place bollards, railings, traffic lights, a no-entry sign, and bicycles beside a corner bistro, with sparse trees and cafe furniture. Keep people and vehicles almost absent and terminate the flat district with abruptly cut blocks and plain courtyard shells.
